lesson.headline: JLPT N3 (Intermediate) — Honorifics (Keigo) & Formal Speech
lesson.lead: Bridging everyday speech with polite, business-grade Japanese. Developing expertise in respectful and humble verbs, expectations, and targeted efforts.
bullets: Keigo Classifications: Respectful Sonkeigo (elevates actions of superiors) vs Humble Kenjougo (lowers actions of oneself to show modesty).
Respectful (Sonkeigo): いらっしゃる (irassharu - to go/come/be), おっしゃる (ossharu - to say), 召し上がる (meshiagaru - to eat/drink).
Humble (Kenjougo): いただく (itadaku - to eat/drink/receive), 申し上げる (moushiageru - to say), 伺う (ukagau - to visit/ask).
Nuance Particles: 〜はずだ (hazu da - expected/should be based on objective reasons), 〜ようにする (youni suru - try/make an effort to establish a habit).

quizzes.q: Which humble (Kenjougo) verb is used to replace the casual verbs "食べる" (to eat) or "もらう" (to receive)?
quizzes.explain: いただく (itadaku) is the humble verb used to express eating, drinking, or receiving from a superior. 召し上がる is respectful.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence with the appropriate intermediate expectation grammar: "The train is scheduled for 3:00, so it ___ arrive soon" (来る___だ).
quizzes.explain: 〜はずだ (hazu da) denotes a logical expectation based on objective evidence: "It should arrive soon."

quizzes.q: What does the grammar construction "〜ようにする" (youni suru) indicate?
quizzes.explain: 〜ようにする (youni suru) signifies making a conscious, continuous effort to do something or establish a healthy habit. E.g., 毎日野菜を食べるようにしています.

quizzes.q: Identify the correct reading of the N3 intermediate Kanji compound "技術" (technology / skill).
quizzes.explain: 技術 is read as "ぎじゅつ" (gijutsu), combining 技 (skill/craft) and 術 (technique/method).

quizzes.q: Which grammar connector denotes "for the sake of" or "in order to" (e.g. "studying for the sake of the exam")?
quizzes.explain: 〜ために (tame ni) indicates a purpose, goal, or benefit: "for the sake of / in order to". It takes a dictionary verb or noun + の.

quizzes.q: What does the particle "〜ばかり" (bakari) mean when placed directly after the past tense Ta-form of a verb (e.g. 食べたばかり)?
quizzes.explain: When 〜ばかり is paired with a past-tense verb (Verb-たばかり), it indicates that the action has just been completed: "just finished doing".

quizzes.q: What is the meaning of the grammar pattern "〜わけがない"? (Context word: 学生)
options: there is no way that / it is impossible that
quizzes.explain: The N3 pattern 〜わけがない means "there is no way that / it is impossible that".
